- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.53) and model shows rising trend, check for mean reversion; if price has been above 70–75 for 5+ days, cap forecast at 75–78 to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.80 to 0.00), model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day from day 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for suppressed market sentiment.
